subject: Heritage Capital — FFIEC readiness / evidence deliverables kickoff
messages:
From: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@heritage-cap.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@heritage-cap.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Heritage Capital — FFIEC readiness info request

Soojin — thanks again for the quick intro last week. Per our compliance steering committee, we need to start gathering vendor evidence to support an FFIEC-style operational resilience review. I’ve attached a spreadsheet with our questions (Heritage_RFP_Questions_v1.xlsx). To get the ball rolling we need confirmation on the following deliverables and a realistic delivery timeline by close of business Friday (5/22):

- Current SOC 2 Type II report (if available) and instructions for secured access
- High-level architecture diagram(s) showing isolation between hosted, dedicated and private deployments
- Disaster recovery / BCP runbook excerpt describing RTO/RPO targets and DR test cadence
- Data retention and deletion policies specific to financial data and audit logs
- Key management (KMS/HSM) overview and third-party KMS integrations (if any)
- Controls mapping to vendor questionnaire (FFIEC-style control IDs are in the sheet)

We anticipate this will be distributed across procurement, legal and the bank’s resilience team — I’ve CC’d procurement. If any deliverables need longer than a week, please flag which items and estimated dates.

We’d also like to schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the spreadsheet and agree owners. Are you available 5/19 in the morning?

Thanks,
Sarah Cole
Director, Vendor Risk — Heritage Capital
attachments: Heritage_RFP_Questions_v1.xlsx
From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@heritage-cap.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Heritage Capital — FFIEC readiness info request

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear asks and the spreadsheet. We can support this scope; appreciate the target dates. Proposed immediate plan:

1) Mutual action plan (MAP) — we will confirm owners and rough deliverable dates by EOD 5/18
2) Package delivery — we’ll produce a consolidated evidence index PDF (redacted as needed) plus itemized artifacts for your review by 5/29 for the initial tranche
3) Call — 30 minutes on 5/19 to align on scoping (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and clarify KMS scope

Quick clarifying questions:
- For "key management" do you require key material export for on-prem/private deployments, or is a KMS architecture and attestation sufficient?
- Are you able to accept redacted network diagrams (traffic flows and VLAN segmentation) — we typically provide redacted diagrams for hosted/dedicated but show full diagrams under NDA for private/on-prem reviews.

Next steps from our side (we’ll take these actions today):
- Assemble SOC 2 access instructions and a redacted evidence index (redwood-ffiec-evidence-index.pdf) — owner: Marcus Lin
- Prepare architecture diagram set and high-level DR runbook excerpt — owner: Laura Bennett
- Map controls in your spreadsheet to our control families and flag any gaps — owner: Soojin Lee

We’re available 5/19 at 10:00 AM ET or 11:30 AM ET for the walkthrough; let me know what works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai
attachments: redwood-ffiec-evidence-index.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@heritage-cap.com>, procurement@heritage-cap.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Heritage Capital — FFIEC readiness info request — deliverables and owners (internal)

Team — quick internal note with owners and estimated dates so we can confirm to Heritage by EOD. I’ve kept the list tight to reduce back-and-forth: 

- SOC 2 Type II (access instructions only): owner Marcus Lin — ETA 5/19 (access URL + short README + SOC2-access-instructions.txt)
- Evidence index (redacted): owner Soojin Lee — ETA 5/22 (redwood-ffiec-evidence-index.pdf)
- Network & infra diagrams (redacted for hosted/dedicated): owner Laura Bennett — ETA 5/29 (we will note that full diagrams require NDA and/or private deployment access)
- DR runbook excerpt, RTO/RPO values and test history: owner Laura Bennett — ETA 5/29
- Control mapping (spreadsheet with cross-reference to their FFIEC IDs): owner Soojin Lee — ETA 5/22 (FFIEC_Evidence_Checklist_v2.xlsx)

Notes / questions for legal & product: 
- Private/on-prem customers: some artifacts (full encryption key handling, raw audit logs) may require a different legal posture — flag for legal review if Heritage wants raw artifacts.
- We should include a short paragraph on how we isolate customer data across deployment modes and where audit logs are retained and for how long (default retention + options).

Attachments I’ll drop into the shared drive for the package: FFIEC_Evidence_Checklist_v2.xlsx, SOC2-access-instructions.txt

I’ll sync with Soojin for the call (10:00 AM ET looks good).

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference
attachments: FFIEC_Evidence_Checklist_v2.xlsx; SOC2-access-instructions.txt
From: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@heritage-cap.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, procurement@heritage-cap.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:47:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Heritage Capital — FFIEC readiness info request

Soojin / Marcus / Laura — thanks, that plan looks good. 10:00 AM ET on 5/19 works for us; invite accepted. A couple of quick asks ahead of the call so our steering committee can prepare: 

- Please mark the SOC 2 access instructions as "read-only" and include the date range covered by the report.
- Add an explicit line item in the control mapping for "audit log retention and tamper protection" (it’s a high-priority item for us).
- We will need a redacted network diagram set in the initial package; if the NDA route is needed for full diagrams we’ll get that started post-call.

One more item: can you include a brief summary (1–2 paragraphs) of your fallback/failover behavior when model-serving capacity is constrained (e.g., model variant fallback, regional failover)? That helps our resilience reviewers understand graceful degradation.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Looking forward to the call.

Best —
Sarah Cole
Director, Vendor Risk — Heritage Capital
attachments: none
